key_insight: In hypersonic blunt-nose boundary layers, stronger nose bluntness and cooler walls generally intensify receptivity by boosting stagnation vorticity, while lift-up effects change more modestly.
engineering_relevance: These scaling laws help predict how wall heating and nose geometry influence early transition in hypersonic vehicle boundary layers.
method: Used a shock-fitting harmonic linearised Navier–Stokes (SF-HLNS) framework.
Applied a three-step asymptotic model to separate stagnation vorticity generation from downstream non-modal evolution.
Examined seven case studies to derive scaling with Reynolds number (R) and wall temperature (T_w).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports seven detailed case studies and explicit scaling laws linking receptivity efficiency to nose bluntness and wall temperature.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on asymptotic and linearized analysis, so applicability may be limited when nonlinear effects or real-flight uncertainties become significant.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part III: effects of wall temperature and nose bluntness
